{{Wireless adapter |brand=Quetec |model=ASW2201 |revision= |upc= |ean= |asin= |price= |est_release_date= |fcc_date=12/24/2003 |manuf_country=Taiwan |manuf= |manuf_model= |manuf_rev= |if=PCMCIA (16-bit) |vendor_id=0000 |device_id=0000 |subvendor_id= |subdevice_id= |fcc_id=ROL-ASW2201 |ic_id= |chip1_brand=WavePlus |chip1_model=WP1200 |chip2_brand=RFMD |chip2_model=RF2958 |chip3_brand= |chip3_model= |flags=schematics |ant_conn= |802dot11_protocols=b |txchains= |rxchains= |sstreams= |oui=00:0E:8B |lin_driver= |win_driver= }} Was sold as a ''SoftGate'' Client/AP device.
'''WavePlus''' WP1200 PCMCIA schematics are included in the FCC documents.
The ''SoftGate'' drivers can be downloaded [http://www.wikidevi.wi-cat.ru/files/Drivers/Quetec/Setup_pcmcia.zip here].
The device is recognized in Windows as a...<small> *PCMCIA\WavePlus_Technology-WLAN_PC_Card_WP1200-63AF *PCMCIA\WavePlus_Technology-WLAN_PC_Card_WP1200-0000-0000</small>
The device looks identical to the [[Actiontec 802CI3]].
On the [http://www.netstumbler.org/hardware/wanted-your-fcc-id-s-t14778-75.html#p141600 NetStumbler FCC ID list thread].
"WavePlus Technology" and "D02-RM-00A" is silkscreened on the back of the board in the FCC photos.
